content: Nystatin is generally well tolerated, even when used for extended periods. However, oral irritation and sensitization have been observed in some cases. In terms of gastrointestinal side effects, patients have reported experiencing diarrhea, which in one instance included bloody diarrhea. Nausea, vomiting, and general gastrointestinal upset or disturbances have also been documented. From a dermatologic perspective, the development of rashes, including urticaria (hives), has been reported, though these occurrences are rare. Extremely rarely, cases of Stevens-Johnson syndrome, a severe and potentially life-threatening skin reaction, have been associated with nystatin use.
